text:
The Florida Panthers got to St. Louis before the FAA's nationwide ground stop on Friday, according to the AP, which is more than some teams can say this weekend. They arrive on the back of a comeback: down three goals to Detroit on Thursday, they scored four unanswered and won 5-4. They have done it without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, both out with knee injuries and both reported close to returning (ESPN's estimates are Nov. 27 and Nov. 21). In the five games since they went out, Matthew Tkachuk has moved up beside Sam Reinhart and his brother Brady, and Lars Eller is playing 17 minutes a night, up from about 13.

There are milestones everywhere on this roster. Reinhart is one point from 700 for his career, and NHL.com noted this week that he just moved into second on the Panthers' all-time goals list. Matthew Tkachuk is two points from 700, riding a six-game point streak built entirely on assists (eight of them). Radko Gudas plays his 900th game. The one habit that keeps games close is the penalty box: Florida takes 5.5 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents power plays.

St. Louis has been living on its goalie. Joel Hofer made 29 saves (per NHL.com) in Thursday's 1-0 shootout win in Utah, a double shutout settled in the eighth round, and he's 9.7 goals better than expected this season, .926 overall and .932 over his last five starts. The skaters haven't matched him: the Blues had 44% of the expected goals, our measure of chance quality, over their last five games. Meanwhile, the Jordan Binnington trade talk keeps running (Pro Hockey Rumors and Sportskeeda among others), which tells you who the starter is right now. Jake Neighbours plays his 300th game, and Dylan Holloway has gone nine games without a goal on 3.7 expected.

Our numbers see a close game: 3.13 expected goals for Florida, 3.06 for St. Louis. Florida's playoff chances sit at 62%, St. Louis's at 35%.
headline: Panthers rally again, still without Barkov
